sections.h2: Which selling routes suit a West Melbourne owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
Three routes exist for a West Melbourne owner: a traditional listing, a cash purchase, or an investor who buys with no repairs requested. Each one trades speed against price, and the choice depends on the state of the roof and systems, how fast you need the money, and whether anything is owed against the title.

  • Agent listing: usually the highest sale price, but showings, repairs and waiting on a buyer's mortgage add weeks.
  • Cash buyer or investor: fewer contingencies and timing you can often pick, though the price tends to run lower.
  • Sale after a repair push: worth it only when the work is cosmetic and cheap, because permits and inspections take time.

Whichever route you pick, get the terms on paper and check who pays for the deed tax, title search and recording. In Florida those costs are negotiable between the parties, so they belong in the contract rather than in a verbal promise.

sections.h2: Where is West Melbourne and how did the city start?
sections.html:
West Melbourne sits in east central Florida in Brevard County, and the municipal history page places it about fifty miles south of the Kennedy Space Center. It was created in 1959, and that page says the founding aim was to avoid annexation into the City of Melbourne and to prevent the levying of ad valorem taxes.

Growth since then has been steep. The page counts 3,050 people in 1970 and 25,924 in 2020. It also records that the first annual audit showed revenues of $13,578, compared with $37,028,775 in revenues in the 2019-2020 audit, a measure of how far city services have grown.

One practical effect follows for sellers. Many West Melbourne homes were built during the decades of rapid growth, so buyers and inspectors often look closely at roofs, air conditioning and electrical work. Buyers who pay cash tend to price those items in rather than ask you to fix them.

sections.h2: Who provides water and sewer service to a West Melbourne home?
sections.html:
The city runs the utility. According to its history page, West Melbourne buys its water from the City of Melbourne and sells it to customers through lines and meters the city owns, while a private contractor operates the wastewater treatment system.

The page counts more than 10,000 water and sewer customers. If your home is on city sewer, the closing agent will want a final utility reading and a clear account. A property still on a septic tank is a different case, so tell any buyer early which system serves the house.

The city's building page also mentions sewer tie-in inspections, which are scheduled Monday through Thursday only. If a prior owner connected to sewer, ask the Building Department for the permit record so a buyer can see the work was inspected.

sections.h2: What does the West Melbourne Building Department require before a sale?
sections.html:
Unpermitted work can surface when a buyer's inspector or lender asks about it. The Building Department page says projects that start without an approved permit, where one is required, can face code enforcement proceedings.

The page also covers a 2026 Florida change. It says House Bill 803 took effect July 1, 2026 and allows certain permit exemptions for small home improvement projects under $7,500, for single family homes, duplexes and townhomes outside flood zones. Electrical, plumbing, structural work (including exterior doors, windows, roofing and sheds), mechanical and gas work still need a permit regardless of cost. An exemption must be requested in writing before work begins.

sections.h2: Can a buyer rent out a West Melbourne house?
sections.html:
Yes, but the city expects a business tax receipt for rentals. Its Business Tax Receipts page links a separate rental application, and it says businesses must hold a receipt that shows the owner has registered and paid local tax.

The page says renewal payments must be received by September 30 to avoid penalties, and that a change in ownership requires a new application plus the deed or a bill of sale. Where the house has tenants, expect the buyer to file fresh. The Finance Department answers questions at 321-327-6614 or 321-327-6616.

If you are the landlord, give the buyer your current rental receipt and tell the tenant about the sale. Whoever wants the house empty should settle that in the contract.

sections.h2: How do Brevard County property taxes affect selling in West Melbourne?
sections.html:
One Brevard County bill carries every levy on a West Melbourne parcel. The Brevard County Tax Collector's page explains that the Property Appraiser sets value, the commissioners, school board, city and other bodies set millage, and a mill is a charge of one dollar on each thousand dollars of value.

That page also says bills go to the owner's last address of record, that escrow lenders normally request the bill themselves, and that an owner who gets no bill must still ask for the amount and pay before delinquency. The office number printed there is (321) 264-6969.

  • January 1 is the assessment date, and the owner must make the home a permanent residence by then to claim homestead.
  • The homestead exemption applies only while the home is your permanent residence and not rented out.
  • After a sale, the assessed value resets to just value the next January 1 for the new owner, so a buyer should not assume your tax figure carries over.

State revenue guidance puts the delinquency date at April 1. Since bills arrive after the year ends, the closing agent splits the current year's tax between seller and buyer, so ask to see that line in writing.

sections.h2: What closing costs apply to a Florida deed in West Melbourne?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax on deeds. The statute sets the rate at $0.70 for every $100 of price paid, and state revenue guidance makes every party to the document liable, whoever agrees to pay. Collection happens when the clerk records the deed.

Clerk recording charges are set by Section 28.24: $5.00 for the opening page and $4.00 for every later page, plus a $1.00 and 50 cent trust fund charge and a technology charge of $4 per page. An itemized settlement statement from the closing agent gives the true figures.

A cash offer does not remove these costs. It changes who negotiates them, so compare offers by net proceeds on the final statement, not by the headline number.

faqs.q: Can I sell my West Melbourne house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, offering it as-is is allowed. Inspections can bring repair requests from a lender or retail buyer; a cash buyer taking it as-is typically folds condition into the price. Ask the Building Department about any open permits first.

faqs.q: Does West Melbourne charge its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: The deed tax is $0.70 per $100 of price, collected by the clerk at recording. Check the draft settlement statement for any other charge.

faqs.q: Are permits needed for minor fixes made before listing?
faqs.a: Frequently. Florida House Bill 803 can exempt some small projects under $7,500 on single family homes outside flood zones, but electrical, plumbing, roofing and other structural work still need a permit. Request any exemption in writing before work begins.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The buyer submits a new business tax receipt application with the deed or bill of sale. Contact the city Finance Department at 321-327-6614 to confirm the steps for your property.

faqs.q: When are Brevard County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Florida Department of Revenue guidance says unpaid taxes become delinquent that day and certificates are sold by June 1. Closing splits the sale year's bill between the parties.
